clusters.state_of_play: The US has launched a fourth consecutive night of strikes on Iran, hitting targets including Bandar Abbas, Qeshm island, and Ahvaz, and has reimposed a naval blockade on all Iranian ports. In a first, the US used sea drones in combat to strike an Iranian submarine and ship maintenance facility near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has retaliated by attacking ships and US Gulf allies, with Jordan, Kuwait, and Bahrain all reporting Iranian strikes; Jordan shot down three Iranian missiles. Iran claims to have killed 3 US service members in Kuwait, while the official US death toll stands at 14, including a Navy pilot killed in a helicopter crash in the Arabian Sea in early July. Oil prices have surged, with Brent crude above $87 per barrel. President Trump says the blockade is designed to starve Iran of oil revenue; Iran refuses to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Dubai has announced plans to build a new port to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

clusters.state_of_play: China and North Korea are marking the 65th anniversary of their friendship treaty. North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song traveled to Beijing, met with Xi Jinping, and Kim Jong-un and Xi exchanged messages pledging deeper strategic cooperation. Separately, Kim Jong-un convened a rare military commission meeting where he denounced corruption in the military, announced plans to boost North Korea's nuclear force in quality and quantity, and ordered a radical expansion of espionage activities targeting South Korea. South Korea has separately voiced concern that North Korean actions along the DMZ constitute a breach of the 1953 armistice agreement. In a related development, China has put Chinese-born American seismologist Youlin Chen on trial after nearly two years of detention; Chen published US-funded research on detecting North Korean nuclear tests and worked as a US government contractor for the State Department and Air Force Research Lab. China's foreign ministry has rejected claims of 'wrongful detention' while not denying that Chen is imprisoned. Chen's wife Yufang Rong is publicly appealing to Trump to help bring him home. New reporting reveals that Trump made a direct personal appeal to Xi Jinping for Chen's release, which went unanswered. Separately, a major Iranian newspaper has published a threat of retaliation against German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, drawing concern from German politicians and a cautious response from the German government. In technology and finance developments: CXMT, China's leading memory chip maker and a linchpin of its AI ambitions, is planning a ~$10B IPO in Shanghai. Oracle is leading a bid to supply Japan with air-gapped top-secret cloud services, under US pressure on Tokyo to tighten data security. Japan's government bond market is selling off amid policy normalization and fiscal concerns, with some experts flagging renewed investor opportunity.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: The UK and EU have signed a post-Brexit Gibraltar treaty at a Brussels ceremony, removing the land border between Gibraltar and Spain and allowing Gibraltar residents to cross using residence cards and Spanish citizens using government ID. The treaty came into effect at midnight, accompanied by a symbolic ceremony and large crowds crossing freely. The old chain-link border fence has been physically torn down, Spanish border checks have been relocated to the international airport and seaport, and Gibraltar is in effect becoming part of the Schengen zone via the EU entry system. Brits entering Gibraltar from Spain will now be fingerprinted under the new arrangements. Tory and Reform MPs are warning this represents a foreign policy 'betrayal' and that Falklands sovereignty could be Labour's next concession. Andy Burnham has secured 349 Labour MP nominations — including all eligible cabinet members — making it impossible for any rival to challenge him, and is confirmed as Britain's next Prime Minister, expected to take office on 20 July. Burnham has pledged a 'broad church' cabinet and party culture, is considering a larger autumn Budget with allies lobbying for a land tax, public control of utilities and expanded devolution. A new Real Rates Reform Alliance is now also pressing him to go further on business rates reform, calling for a 2% online sales tax to fund a 37% cut in rates for physical retailers. He plans to scrap David Lammy's jury-trial abolition proposals. He voted to back immigration curbs at the Immigration and Asylum Bill's second reading despite a threatened left-wing revolt. Burnham has not uttered a word in the Commons chamber since being sworn in as Makerfield MP on 22 June. Tories are demanding Parliament delay its summer recess to scrutinise him before he takes office. clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: The two Fontainebleau forest fires, which have burned just over 2,000 hectares south of Paris since Sunday, have been declared 'contained' — confined within their perimeter — by local Prefect Pierre Ory on Tuesday evening, though they are not yet extinguished. Police have arrested two people suspected of deliberately starting the fire; investigators found ten ignition points near the origin. Around 1,000 people have been evacuated. Officials described the blaze as of 'exceptional scale', with road and rail links disrupted. Some 400 firefighters and two waterbombing aircraft have been deployed. The fire coincides with France's third heatwave since May, which forced early closures of the Eiffel Tower, Louvre, and Musée d'Orsay, and led many towns to cancel Bastille Day fireworks displays.

The treaty came into effect at midnight, accompanied by a symbolic ceremony and large crowds crossing freely. The old chain-link border fence has been physically torn down, Spanish border checks have been relocated to the international airport and seaport, and Gibraltar is in effect becoming part of the Schengen zone via the EU entry system. He plans to scrap David Lammy's jury-trial abolition proposals. He voted to back immigration curbs at the Immigration and Asylum Bill's second reading despite a threatened left-wing revolt. clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

items.title: Texas Faces Potentially ‘Catastrophic’ Amounts of Rain

ledger.what_new: Texas faces potentially catastrophic rainfall; intense overnight storms with more flooding forecast statewide.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. More than 20 million people across at least 14 states from Colorado to Pennsylvania are under flood watches through Saturday. The flash-flood threat is continuing into Sunday, extending from Tennessee to West Virginia. The threat has now expanded to Texas, where flash flood warnings have been issued across the Texas Hill Country; local authorities are already reporting cars stranded in high water and forecasters warn of potentially catastrophic rainfall with isolated totals of up to 15 inches possible. Families have drawn comparisons to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in central Texas from the prior year. Separately, days of torrential monsoon rain have triggered major flooding in Bangladesh, killing dozens and leaving millions stranded in the south-east of the country, with food supply shortages reported.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. More than 20 million people across at least 14 states from Colorado to Pennsylvania are under flood watches through Saturday. The flash-flood threat is continuing into Sunday, extending from Tennessee to West Virginia. The threat has now expanded to Texas, where flash flood warnings have been issued across the Texas Hill Country; local authorities are already reporting cars stranded in high water and forecasters warn of potentially catastrophic rainfall with isolated totals of up to 15 inches possible. Families have drawn comparisons to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in central Texas from the prior year. Separately, days of torrential monsoon rain have triggered major flooding in Bangladesh, killing dozens and leaving millions stranded in the south-east of the country, with food supply shortages reported.

items.title: Map reveals areas most at risk to wildfires as heatwave sparks huge infernos across the UK

ledger.what_new: Met Office Fire Severity Index identifies southern England, Chichester and Bognor Regis as highest wildfire risk areas.
ledger.unique: Met Office FSI map naming specific high-risk UK locations.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

clusters.title: A rainy start to the week in Houston comes with flooding risks

items.title: A rainy start to the week in Houston comes with flooding risks

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. The treaty came into effect at midnight, accompanied by a symbolic ceremony and large crowds crossing freely. The old chain-link border fence has been physically torn down, Spanish border checks have been relocated to the international airport and seaport, and Gibraltar is in effect becoming part of the Schengen zone via the EU entry system. Brits entering Gibraltar from Spain will now be fingerprinted under the new arrangements. Tory and Reform MPs are warning this represents a foreign policy 'betrayal' and that Falklands sovereignty could be Labour's next concession. Andy Burnham has secured 349 Labour MP nominations — including all eligible cabinet members — making it impossible for any rival to challenge him, and is confirmed as Britain's next Prime Minister, expected to take office on 20 July. Burnham has pledged a 'broad church' cabinet and party culture, is considering a larger autumn Budget with allies lobbying for a land tax, public control of utilities and expanded devolution. A new Real Rates Reform Alliance is now also pressing him to go further on business rates reform, calling for a 2% online sales tax to fund a 37% cut in rates for physical retailers. He plans to scrap David Lammy's jury-trial abolition proposals. He voted to back immigration curbs at the Immigration and Asylum Bill's second reading despite a threatened left-wing revolt. Burnham has not uttered a word in the Commons chamber since being sworn in as Makerfield MP on 22 June. Tories are demanding Parliament delay its summer recess to scrutinise him before he takes office. The Reform UK/Farage financial scrutiny story continues: the £5m crypto donor is now linked to Tether, a giant and secretive cryptocurrency firm that Farage has publicly championed. clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with nationality now confirmed: five Britons, three Belgians, one French national, and one Spanish national among the dead; DNA identification was required for badly burned victims. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. In the UK, major incidents have been declared in North Wales and in Glossop, Derbyshire in the Peak District, with at least 10 wildfires burning across Wales and 19 separate wildfires being tackled across the UK overall. A wildfire near Conwy Mountain prompted evacuation of 36 homes. A 20-year-old woman, Shania Care-Slede, has been charged with aggravated arson in connection with a UK moor fire for which a major incident was declared. The Met Office's Fire Severity Index identifies parts of southern England — including around Chichester and Bognor Regis in West Sussex — as most at risk. An 'exceptional' wildfire warning has been issued for parts of the UK as a heatwave, now entering its second week in some areas, is forecast to last at least another week; hosepipe bans are in effect. The National Fire Chiefs Council warned that hot dry weather 'significantly increases wildfire risk.' Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.' In a separate legal development, Sánchez's brother David has been banned from holding public office for nine years after being convicted of administrative misconduct relating to his hiring by a socialist-led council in Extremadura.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed an executive order imposing the first statewide moratorium on new large (hyperscaler) data centers for one year, citing energy grid, environmental, and ratepayer cost concerns, including ensuring New Yorkers do not bear costs of transmission and infrastructure build-outs, while state lawmakers draft a nation-leading regulatory framework. The moratorium is drawing backlash from critics who say it will further damage upstate New York's already sagging economy. The action follows a growing left-wing grassroots campaign, backed by Sanders-aligned progressives, opposing AI data center expansion. Similar grassroots opposition is emerging elsewhere, including Paulding County, Georgia, where furious homeowners packed standing-room-only county commission meetings and held a protest demanding a local moratorium. Separately, a PJM power auction — covering the nation's largest electrical grid — is projected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses across 13 states as a direct result of data center electricity demand, underscoring the ratepayer cost concerns driving moratorium efforts.

clusters.state_of_play: China and North Korea are marking the 65th anniversary of their friendship treaty. China's foreign ministry has rejected claims of 'wrongful detention' while not denying that Chen is imprisoned. Chen's wife Yufang Rong is publicly appealing to Trump to help bring him home. New reporting reveals that Trump made a direct personal appeal to Xi Jinping for Chen's release, which went unanswered. Separately, a major Iranian newspaper has published a threat of retaliation against German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, drawing concern from German politicians and a cautious response from the German government. In technology and finance developments: CXMT, China's leading memory chip maker and a linchpin of its AI ambitions, is planning a ~$10B IPO in Shanghai. ledger.what_new: Cyclospora was dropped from federal monitoring program last summer due to Trump-era cuts.
ledger.unique: CDC monitoring program cut as causal factor in outbreak detection gap.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

items.title: Parasitic infection outbreak exposes deep cracks in public health

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed an executive order imposing the first statewide moratorium on new large (hyperscaler) data centers for one year, citing energy grid, environmental, and ratepayer cost concerns, including ensuring New Yorkers do not bear costs of transmission and infrastructure build-outs, while state lawmakers draft a nation-leading regulatory framework. The moratorium is drawing backlash from critics who say it will further damage upstate New York's already sagging economy. The action follows a growing left-wing grassroots campaign, backed by Sanders-aligned progressives, opposing AI data center expansion. Similar grassroots opposition is emerging elsewhere, including Paulding County, Georgia, where furious homeowners packed standing-room-only county commission meetings and held a protest demanding a local moratorium. Separately, a PJM power auction — covering the nation's largest electrical grid — is projected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses across 13 states as a direct result of data center electricity demand, underscoring the ratepayer cost concerns driving moratorium efforts.

clusters.state_of_play: A new study estimates more than 2,700 people died from heat-related causes during the UK's exceptionally hot May and June, with roughly 40% of those deaths attributed to climate change. At the peak of the June heatwave, an estimated 440 people per day died over its three-day peak. Researchers warn the worst is yet to come. Separately, the heatwave also boosted UK retail spending in June, with total retail sales up 1.9% year on year and online sales up 5.1%.
